title: Potential midway between +4 nC and −2 nC
caption: Potential is a scalar, so the contributions add with their signs: V = k(4 × 10⁻⁹ − 2 × 10⁻⁹)/0.1 = 180 V. The field there, in contrast, is a vector: both charges push the same way, from + towards −, so E = k(4 + 2) × 10⁻⁹/0.1² = 5393 V m⁻¹, not the difference.
alt: Two point charges 0.2 m apart, +4 nC and −2 nC, with field lines and equipotentials; the midpoint is at 180 V and the field there points from the positive to the negative charge.
description: Two point charges 0.2 m apart: +4 nC on the left and −2 nC on the right, with field lines and equipotential lines.
At the midpoint, 0.1 m from each, the potentials add as numbers: k × 4 nC/0.1 + k × (−2 nC)/0.1 = 180 V.
The fields add as vectors: both point from + to −, so E = 5393 V m⁻¹ towards the −2 nC charge.
